subject: Private/VPC pricing follow-up — token volumes & licensing options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@enterprisenet.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Private/VPC pricing & next steps

Hi Samantha — great call earlier today, thanks for walking me through EnterpriseNet's use cases. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get a clean proposal over to procurement: 

1) Summary of needs (as I heard them)
- Production usage: low-latency document ingestion + agent responses for customer support and internal ops
- Isolation requirement: private VPC deployment with customer-managed networking and KMS
- Observability: 90-day traces + token-level cost reporting

2) Pricing topics we covered to confirm
- Licensing: options are (a) annual subscription (capacity-based) that includes runtime + support, or (b) perpetual license + annual support/maintenance. We typically price private/VPC as a function of committed token throughput + environment count.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 99.5% basic SLAs) vs Premium (24/7, faster response, on-call rotations, dedicated TAM).
- Environment count: we need to know how many isolated environments you want (prod, staging, QA, dev, sandboxes) and whether each needs dedicated capacity.

3) Data we still need from you (helps us hit target unit economics)
- Expected token volume per month (baseline and peak) per environment
- Target $/1M tokens you're budgeting toward (or a monthly/annual budget range)
- Any hard constraints on licensing model (e.g., must be subscription vs one-time license)

Attachments: pricing_workbook_enterprisenet_20270718.xlsx (workbook with sample bands) and EnterpriseNet_MAA_draft_20270718.pdf (mutual action agreement draft).

Next steps
- If you can send the token volume ranges + environment counts today, I’ll get a tailored proposal with two licensing options and the support tier pricing.
- If it helps, I can include ballpark unit economics in the proposal (example: $X per 1M tokens at 6-month commit).

Thanks — talk soon.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@enterprisenet.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@enterprisenet.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Private/VPC pricing & next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from our side: 

Token volumes 
- Baseline (prod): ~20M tokens/month across the customer-support agent flows (these are short responses, lots of small requests)
- Peak/spikes: up to ~60M tokens/month during major releases / campaigns (we expect 2–3x bursts)
- Non-prod (staging + QA + dev): combined ~5M tokens/month (mostly validation and regression tests)

Environment counts
- Prod: 2 dedicated environments (east/west for DR)
- Staging: 1 shared environment
- QA/dev: 2 lightweight sandboxes (shared, low capacity)
- Total distinct environments needing isolation: 5

Budget / unit economics
- We have a procurement target of roughly $15k–$25k / month allocated to this project for inference and support in Year 1.
- We’d like to see pricing that gets us to ~$100–$150 per 1M tokens (ballpark) for private/VPC deployment at our expected commit levels. If the license model requires a large up-front perpetual fee that materially reduces this, procurement will need to see TCO over 3 years.

Other constraints
- KMS integration is required; SOC2 Type II compliance is a must.
- Our security team will need SAML + audit logs visible in the console.

Happy to hop on a follow-up next week if helpful — procurement included on cc.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Product, EnterpriseNet
samantha@enterprisenet.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@enterprisenet.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@enterprisenet.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T17:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Private/VPC pricing & next steps

Samantha — thanks, that is super helpful. Quick follow-up and a couple of concrete numbers so procurement has something to evaluate immediately.

High-level proposal options (ballpark ranges, will formalize in the workbook):
1) Subscription (recommended for most customers) — capacity-based commit
- Model: Monthly committed tokens + optional burst capacity. Private/VPC runs on dedicated pools sized to your commit.
- Example pricing bands (for illustration only):
  - 0–50M committed tokens/mo: $220 / 1M tokens
  - 50–200M committed tokens/mo: $140 / 1M tokens
  - 200M+ committed tokens/mo: $95 / 1M tokens
- Support tiers: Standard (included with subscription) vs Premium (+25%–40% on top of subscription; includes 24/7 support and TAM).

2) Perpetual license + annual support (one-time + O&M) — suitable if you prefer CapEx
- Model: one-time license for runtime + per-node pricing; annual support ~20% of license value. Effective $/1M tokens will depend on utilization; we’ll run a 3-year TCO to compare.

Based on your volumes (20M baseline, 60M peak), the subscription band that fits closest is the 0–50M or if you want to cover peak capacity you'd look at the 50–200M band. To get to your target of ~$100–$150 / 1M tokens we’d likely be in the 50–200M band with a 6–12 month commit and a Premium support adjustment depending on SLAs.

Questions / asks from our side before we finalize the quote:
- Can you confirm whether both prod environments need fully dedicated capacity (i.e., two separate dedicated pools) or if one can be active and the other passive failover? This materially affects node/licensing counts.
- Any hard constraints on commit length (6m vs 12m vs 36m)? Longer commits move you to lower $/1M bands.
- Procurement: if you prefer the perpetual + support route, let us know and we’ll run a 3-year TCO.

I attached an updated pricing_workbook_enterprisenet_20270718.xlsx with sample math for the bands above and a simple TCO tab. I’ll also draft two short proposal options (subscription + perpetual) and include Premium vs Standard support as line items.

Next steps
- Samantha / procurement to confirm: (a) prod env capacity requirement (dedicated vs passive), (b) preferred commit length, (c) confirmation of $/1M target band or monthly budget number to align the proposal.
- I’ll pull together a formal proposal and draft PO-friendly term sheet once you confirm.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for confirmation and can schedule a follow-up call if helpful.

Ben
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: EnterpriseNet — recommended posture before proposal

Ben / Rishi — quick internal note after Ben's draft reply to EnterpriseNet (see thread):

Key asks from customer: token volumes (provided), 5 isolated environments, KMS + SOC2. Procurement has a $15k–$25k/mo target and a target unit cost of ~$100–$150 / 1M tokens.

Recommendation:
- Offer subscription-based capacity commit (12-month) as primary proposal. Use the 50–200M band pricing in the workbook as the basis (we can show examples for 20M baseline vs 60M peak).
- Support: propose Premium as the default for Year 1 given KMS + DR requirements; show Standard as a reduced-cost alternative. Premium = +30% on top of subscription.
- Environment licensing: clarify with customer if the second prod env is active-active or passive. If passive, charge only a smaller HA reserve vs full dedicated pool — this is where we can be flexible on price.
- Discounts / approvals: we can offer up to a 12% commercial discount off the band pricing for a 12-month commit; anything deeper requires director approval.

Action items:
- Ben: ask customer to confirm active vs passive prod requirement and preferred commit length (6/12/36m).
- Rishi: hold margin approval for up to 12% discount; anything beyond route to me.
- I’ll prepare a proposal template and escalate terms to legal for a 3-year TCO/perpetual path if procurement asks.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deals | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
